title: Spelunk protocol
description: Single source of truth for every type that crosses a process boundary: the parsed query (ParsedQuery), the messages between the search panel webview and the extension host, and the JSON-RPC methods between the extension host and the daemon. Run `node protocol/gen.mjs` after editing.

Span.description: Span is a range of UTF-16 offsets into the raw query text.

MessageLine.description: MessageLine is one line of a commit message, with what the query's text terms match in it.

SpanLine.description: SpanLine is a later line of a code match that spans lines, with the part of the match on it (and any other term's matches there).

Range.description: Range is a range of UTF-16 offsets into the text shown on screen.

Hit.description: Hit is a matched Range plus the text term that matched, which picks its highlight color.

hole.description: For a struct: match, the number of the template hole whose code this marks (1 for the first name in the template); absent where the template's own code matched.

HoleValue.description: HoleValue is the code a struct: template's named hole took in one match, its space squeezed and cut short when long.

hole.description: The hole's number, as in Hit.hole.

OpName.description: OpName is an operator's name, the part before the colon.

CaseSetting.description: CaseSetting is how capital letters match when the query has no case: ignored (off), matched (on), or matched only when the query has a capital letter (smart).

ResultOrder.description: ResultOrder is how current files are sorted: best match first, by repo, file path and line (file or file:asc A to Z, file:desc Z to A), or by when each file last changed (recent or recent:desc newest first, recent:asc oldest first).

RankReason.description: RankReason is why best-match order put a file where it is: it defines a searched name or is open in the editor, or it was moved down as a test, vendored or generated file, or as one VS Code's excludes hide (shown by excludes:no). Absent when nothing stands out or the order is path.

SinceRevision.description: SinceRevision is how a file found at a revision differs in the current files: its content changed, it was deleted, or it was renamed (renamedTo says to what).

Match.description: Match says how a value was written: bare (literal), quoted (phrase), /regex/, a path glob such as *.go (f: and repo: only), or a struct: template of code with :[holes] (structural).

Mode.description: Mode is what a query searches: current files or Git history.

Severity.description: Severity is how serious a Diagnostic is; only errors stop a search.

TextEdit.description: TextEdit replaces a span of the query text.

Fix.description: Fix is a titled set of edits that repairs or rewrites the query.

Diagnostic.description: Diagnostic is a problem the parser found, with fixes the user can apply.

Resolved.description: Resolved is a friendlier label for an operator value, such as an author's full name.

Node.description: Node is one node of the parsed query tree.

contentOnly.description: true for a content: or struct: term, which matches the text of files (or a commit's changed lines) and never file names or commit messages.

Globals.description: Globals are the query-wide operators case:, word:, count:, type:, order: and at:, or null when absent.

case.description: the query's case: value: yes, no or smart (match case only when the query has a capital letter).

word.description: the query's word: value, yes or no; absent when the query doesn't say.

match.description: the query's match: value: fuzzy also finds file names that have a word's letters in order, exact matches the text only; absent when the query doesn't say.

excludes.description: the query's excludes: value: yes leaves out the files VS Code's files.exclude and search.exclude hide, no keeps them; absent when the query doesn't say, which means yes unless spelunk.search.useExcludeSettings is off.

order.description: the query's order: value, such as best, file:desc or recent:asc; absent when the query doesn't say.

at.description: the query's at: value as written: the tag, branch, commit or time whose files it searches; absent when the query doesn't say.

ParsedQuery.description: ParsedQuery is the parser's output: the query tree, its global operators and its diagnostics.

hasCapital.description: whether a text term, sym: or msg: value has a capital letter, so smart case matches case. In a regex, only literal letters count: \W and \p{Lu} don't.

Root.description: Root is a workspace folder; its id is the first 12 hex digits of sha256(path).

RootExcludes.description: RootExcludes are the glob patterns VS Code hides in one workspace folder, as files.exclude and search.exclude write them: relative to the folder.

ExcludePattern.description: ExcludePattern is one enabled files.exclude or search.exclude entry: a VS Code glob, and its when clause if it has one, e.g. $(basename).ts to hide a file only beside a sibling of that name.

Settings.description: Settings are the spelunk.* settings the daemon needs.

caseSensitive.description: the spelunk.search.caseSensitive setting: how a query without case: treats capital letters.

wholeWord.description: the spelunk.search.wholeWord setting: match text terms only as whole words unless the query says word:no.

match.description: the spelunk.search.match setting: fuzzy lets a query without match: also find file names by a word's letters in order. Absent means exact.

mergedBranches.description: the spelunk.index.mergedBranches setting: history also reads the commits that merges brought in from other branches, each by its own author and dated by its merge, and shows a merge as only what it changed itself. Absent means false: the branch's own line only, each merge holding its whole branch.

notebookOutputs.description: the spelunk.index.notebookOutputs setting: also search the text that a Jupyter notebook's code cells printed or returned. Absent means false: only cells' source is searched.

order.description: the spelunk.results.order setting: how a query without order: sorts current files. Absent means best.

contextLines.description: the spelunk.results.contextLines setting: how many lines each code result shows before and after its match, 0 to 3. Absent means 0.

timeLimitMs.description: the spelunk.search.timeLimitMs setting: how long one search runs before it returns what it found so far, marked truncated. Absent means 2000.

vendoredFolders.description: the spelunk.index.vendoredFolders setting: names of folders, at any depth, whose files is:vendored matches and ranking puts last. Absent means vendor, node_modules, third_party and dist.

generatedSuffixes.description: the spelunk.index.generatedSuffixes setting: endings of file names that mark files a tool wrote, for is:generated and ranking, besides a @generated or DO NOT EDIT marker near the top. Absent means .pb.go, _gen.go, .gen.go, .gen.ts, _pb2.py, _pb2_grpc.py, _pb2.pyi, .min.js and .min.css.

codeownersFiles.description: the spelunk.index.codeownersFiles setting: where to look for a repo's CODEOWNERS file, relative to its root, the first found winning. Absent means GitHub's .github/CODEOWNERS, CODEOWNERS and docs/CODEOWNERS.

editorExcludes.description: VS Code's files.exclude and search.exclude for each workspace folder, enabled patterns only, while spelunk.search.useExcludeSettings is on: searches leave out the files they hide unless the query says excludes:no. Absent or empty hides nothing.

commitCheckSeconds.description: the spelunk.index.commitCheckSeconds setting: how often to ask Git whether HEAD moved, which brings new commits into history search and watches. Absent means 5.

shareWindow.description: the spelunk.agent.shareWindow setting: let the spelunk command and AI agents on this computer search this window's roots, through a socket only the user can open. Absent means false.

agentTimeLimitMs.description: the spelunk.agent.timeLimitMs setting: how long a search from the spelunk command or an agent runs before it returns what it found so far, marked truncated. Absent means 30000.

LastCommit.description: LastCommit is the newest commit that touched a file.

FileStat.description: FileStat is one file changed by a commit.

oldPath.description: The file's path before this commit renamed it to path; absent when the commit didn't rename it.

currentPath.description: The file's path now, after renames made by later commits, when it differs from path.

resolution.description: With index.mergedBranches, whether these lines of a merge are how it resolved a conflict, rather than its own edit.

SymbolKind.description: SymbolKind is what a symbol definition is.

ResultItem.description: ResultItem is one search result: a file name, a code line, a symbol or a commit.

modifiedAt.description: In a search sorted by when files last changed, when the file was last saved: for a file outside Git, or one with uncommitted changes. Absent otherwise.

owners.description: Who the repo's CODEOWNERS file says owns the file, as it writes them; absent when nobody does or the repo has no CODEOWNERS file.

sinceRevision.description: For a search at a revision (at:), how the file differs now: changed, or deleted since; absent when it is the same now, and in every other search.

renamedTo.description: For a search at a revision (at:), the file's path now when sinceRevision is renamed.

owners.description: Who the repo's CODEOWNERS file says owns the file, as it writes them; absent when nobody does or the repo has no CODEOWNERS file.

lastCommit.description: In a search sorted by when files last changed, the newest commit that touched the file, unless it has uncommitted changes. Absent otherwise.

dirty.description: In a search sorted by when files last changed, whether the file has uncommitted changes. Absent otherwise.

modifiedAt.description: In a search sorted by when files last changed, when the file was last saved: for a file outside Git, or one with uncommitted changes. Absent otherwise.

spanLines.description: When the match spans lines (a regex with \n, or a struct: template), the lines after line that it runs onto, in order: at most 10, so a longer match ends at endLine past the last of them. Absent for a match within one line.

endLine.description: The last line a match that spans lines ends on; present with spanLines.

holes.description: For a struct: match, what each named hole of the template took, in template order, each hole once; absent otherwise.

cell.description: For a result in a Jupyter notebook: the cell it is in, and its line there. line counts lines of the notebook's text, each cell's source in turn.

within.description: For a use found inside a definition (kind:, symbol: or a word with ref:, content:, struct: or a regex across lines): the innermost definition the query kept that holds the line.

contextBefore.description: The lines just above the match, top first, when the contextLines setting asks for them; fewer near the start of the file.

contextAfter.description: The lines just below the match (below endLine when it spans lines), when the contextLines setting asks for them; fewer near the end of the file.

sinceRevision.description: For a search at a revision (at:), how the file differs now: changed, or deleted since; absent when it is the same now, and in every other search.

renamedTo.description: For a search at a revision (at:), the file's path now when sinceRevision is renamed.

cell.description: For a result in a Jupyter notebook: the cell it is in, and its line there. line counts lines of the notebook's text, each cell's source in turn.

sinceRevision.description: For a search at a revision (at:), how the file differs now: changed, or deleted since; absent when it is the same now, and in every other search.

renamedTo.description: For a search at a revision (at:), the file's path now when sinceRevision is renamed.

inMessage.description: Whether a text term matched the commit's subject or body.

bodyLine.description: The first body line a text term matched, sent when the subject has no match.

parents.description: How many parents the commit has: 2 or more for a merge; absent for 1.

mergedIn.description: With index.mergedBranches, for a commit made on another branch: the sha of the merge that brought it in.

mergedAt.description: When mergedIn was committed, which since: and until: go by for this commit.

Within.description: Within is the definition a code result sits in: its name, kind and lines.

CellPlace.description: CellPlace is where a line of a Jupyter notebook's text is: the cell, 1-based, and the line in it, 1-based. An output line (index.notebookOutputs) names the cell that printed it.

language.description: The canonical language of the cell's text, such as python or markdown; absent for raw cells, outputs and unknown languages.

CellKind.description: CellKind is what a notebook cell holds: code, markdown or raw text, or (index.notebookOutputs) the text a code cell printed.

NotebookCell.description: NotebookCell is one cell of a Jupyter notebook previewed: its number, 1-based, and the lines of the notebook's text it is, from startLine for lineCount lines.

language.description: The canonical language of its text, such as python or markdown; absent for raw cells, outputs and unknown languages.

executionCount.description: The number Jupyter shows beside a code cell that ran; absent when it hasn't run.

outputs.description: What a code cell's outputs are, in order: text it printed or returned, an image, or something else. Only text outputs are ever searched, and only with index.notebookOutputs.

LineHits.description: LineHits are the matches on one preview line.

OutlineSymbol.description: OutlineSymbol is a definition in a file preview's outline. The outline lists the file's definitions top to bottom, each class, type or interface followed by its members.

depth.description: how many classes, types or interfaces it is inside: 0 at the top

DiffLine.description: DiffLine is one line of a diff hunk.

cell.description: In a Jupyter notebook's diff, which diffs its cells' source: the cell the line is in, and its line there, in the notebook before the commit for a removed line and after it otherwise.

Hunk.description: Hunk is one hunk of a commit diff.

Ownership.description: Ownership is who owns a file by its repo's CODEOWNERS file, and which line of it says so.

owners.description: The owners, as the file writes them; empty when the deciding line names none, or no line matches.

file.description: Where the CODEOWNERS file is, relative to the repo: .github/CODEOWNERS

line.description: The line that decides, 1-based; 0 when no line matches the file.

Preview.description: Preview is the right-hand pane's content for a selected result.

focusEndLine.description: The last line of the result when its match spans lines; the preview marks focusLine to focusEndLine. Absent otherwise.

cells.description: For a Jupyter notebook, every cell, in order, so the preview can show each line's cell; lines and focusLine count lines of the notebook's text, each cell's source in turn. Absent for other files.

Facet.description: Facet counts a search's results by one field, biggest bucket first, for the buttons that narrow the results.

more.description: How many smaller buckets were left out

FacetBucket.description: FacetBucket is one value of a facet: how many results have it, and the filter that keeps only them.

label.description: The value as shown, e.g. payments-api, Python, src/, @acme/payments-core, Jane Doe, Sep 2026

filter.description: The filter that keeps only this bucket, as it would be typed, e.g. repo:payments-api; a - before it leaves the bucket out

HiddenNote.description: HiddenNote counts results a filter removed, with a fix that removes the filter.

patterns.description: For VS Code's excludes, the patterns that hid (or, when shown, matched) the results, as written in the settings, e.g. build and dist.

shown.description: Set when the query says excludes:no: count is how many results VS Code's excludes would hide, which show, and undo hides them again.

Completion.description: Completion is an autocomplete suggestion; accepting it applies its edit.

detail.description: What the suggestion means, in a few words: "Last 2 hours", "Python files".

context.description: Facts that help choose it, on a second line: "Since 08:04", "14 files · payments-api, web-checkout".

note.description: A short status shown at the end of the row: "5 files changed", "Indexing 64%".

section.description: A heading shown above this suggestion; the suggestions after it, up to the next section, belong under it.

IndexState.description: IndexState is where one index of a repo stands.

RepoStatus.description: RepoStatus is the indexing state of one repo.

savedAt.description: when the working-tree index being searched was saved, RFC 3339; absent until it is first saved.

reread.description: how many files were re-read since that index was saved: they are searched as they are now.

writer.description: whether this daemon builds and saves the repo's index: false when another VS Code window does, and for the spelunk command's reader.

OpenTarget.description: OpenTarget is where opening a result goes: a file position (path, line, column, length, or to endLine and endColumn for a match that spans lines) or a commit (repoId, sha). A file at a revision (an at: result) also has revision, and opens read-only with the text of revision/text. Lines and columns are 1-based.

endLine.description: Where a match that spans lines ends: the selection runs from line and column to endLine and endColumn.

revision.description: The full sha of the commit whose version of the file opens, for an at: result.

cell.description: For a result in a Jupyter notebook: the cell to open the notebook at, and the line in it. line still counts lines of the notebook's text.

revisionLabel.description: How the revision reads in the editor's title: the at: value (v1.0.0), or the short sha when the search is forgotten.

OpenPosition.description: OpenPosition is where a double-click in a file preview lands, opened instead of the match: the word it selected, from a 1-based line and column (UTF-16), length long.

OpenWhere.description: OpenWhere is which editor group a result opens in, or, for a result at a revision (at:), compare: a diff of the file then against the file now.

watches.description: The watched queries, as in watch/set.

InitializeResult.description: InitializeResult reports the daemon's version and protocol.

WatchSetParams.description: WatchSetParams list the watched queries: after each history update, the daemon runs every one that searches history over the new commits.

WatchCommit.description: WatchCommit is a new commit a watched query matched.

WatchMatchedParams.description: WatchMatchedParams announce the new commits of one repo that a watched query matched, newest first; your own commits are left out. total counts them all; commits lists at most the query's count.

FileChange.description: FileChange is one file event from VS Code's watcher.

DidChangeFilesParams.description: DidChangeFilesParams forward file events from the host; the daemon also lists each repo's files every few minutes, for changes no event told it of.

ParseParams.description: ParseParams ask the daemon to parse the query box.

openFiles.description: the absolute paths of the files open in editor tabs, for is:open.

ParseResult.description: ParseResult is the parsed query plus completions at the cursor.

SearchStartParams.description: SearchStartParams start (or page) a search; the daemon re-parses the text itself.

openFiles.description: the absolute paths of the files open in editor tabs, for is:open.

roots.description: the absolute paths of the roots to search, for a search from the spelunk command or an agent; absent means every open root.

timeLimitMs.description: how long this search runs before it returns what it found so far, marked truncated; absent means the setting (spelunk.search.timeLimitMs).

count.description: how many results to return when the query has no count:; absent means the setting (spelunk.results.count).

SearchResult.description: SearchResult ends a search after its batches.

revisions.description: For an at: search, the commit each searched repo read, in workspace order; absent otherwise.

RevisionInfo.description: RevisionInfo is the commit an at: search read in one repo: its sha and date, or why the repo has none.

sha.description: The commit's full sha; absent when the repo has no such revision.

date.description: When the commit was made (its committer date), RFC 3339; absent with sha.

problem.description: Why the repo was not searched, when it has no such revision: "v9 isn't a tag, branch or commit here", "Not a Git repository".

RevisionTextParams.description: RevisionTextParams ask for the whole text of a file a revision result names.

RevisionText.description: RevisionText is a file's whole text as it was at the revision of a result's ref: for a Jupyter notebook, its JSON, so it opens in the notebook editor.

SearchBatchParams.description: SearchBatchParams stream up to 200 results of a running search.

PreviewParams.description: PreviewParams ask for the preview of a result.

OpenResolveParams.description: OpenResolveParams ask where a result opens.

IndexStatusResult.description: IndexStatusResult is the indexing state of every repo.

ShareHelloResult.description: ShareHelloResult describes a daemon to the spelunk command or an agent that connects to its socket.

reader.description: true for the spelunk command's background reader, false for a VS Code window.

ShareOpenParams.description: ShareOpenParams ask the background reader to serve the saved index of the root that holds path.

path.description: an absolute folder path: a root, or a folder inside one.

RebuildParams.description: RebuildParams name the repo to rebuild, or all when repoId is absent.

ReplacePlanParams.description: ReplacePlanParams ask for every edit that replacing the query's matches in current files would make.

replacement.description: the text each match becomes; for a /regex/ term, $1 or ${name} insert what a group matched.

openFiles.description: the absolute paths of the files open in editor tabs, for is:open.

ReplaceEdit.description: ReplaceEdit replaces one match: a range of UTF-16 offsets into the whole line.

ReplaceLine.description: ReplaceLine is one line to edit: its 1-based number, its whole text as indexed (without the line end), and its edits in order.

ReplaceFile.description: ReplaceFile is one file to edit, with its absolute path.

ReplacePlan.description: ReplacePlan is every edit a replace would make. When it would make more than the daemon plans at once, truncated is set and files is empty.

excluded.description: How many matches are in files VS Code's excludes hide, which the plan leaves alone; absent when none.

Empty.description: Empty is a message with no fields.

Envelope.description: Envelope wraps every message between the webview and the extension host, in both directions.

QueryChangedMessage.description: QueryChangedMessage reports the query box after the typing delay.

asTyped.description: True when the user dismissed the suggestions (Esc or Enter): search the box exactly as typed, including the word at the cursor.

ResultSelectMessage.description: ResultSelectMessage asks for a result's preview.

ResultOpenMessage.description: ResultOpenMessage opens a result in an editor.

ResultsMoreMessage.description: ResultsMoreMessage loads the next page of results.

HelpTryMessage.description: HelpTryMessage runs an example from the help page in the search panel.

PinnedQuery.description: PinnedQuery is a query starred in the empty box, with the name it was given, if any, and whether it is watched.

watch.description: Whether new commits the query matches are announced (query watches); history queries only.

PinnedWatchMessage.description: PinnedWatchMessage starts or stops watching a pinned query for new commits.

UnseenCommits.description: UnseenCommits are the new commits a watched query matched since it last ran: how many, and their shas.

WatchStateMessage.description: WatchStateMessage says which pinned queries can be watched (those that search history) and what each watch found since its query last ran.

ContextSetMessage.description: ContextSetMessage sets how many lines each code result shows around its match (spelunk.results.contextLines).

OrderSetMessage.description: OrderSetMessage sets how results from current files are sorted (spelunk.results.order), from the order menu or the direction arrow in a section title.

RecentRemoveMessage.description: RecentRemoveMessage removes a query from the recent list.

ReplacePreviewMessage.description: ReplacePreviewMessage asks what replacing the query's matches with replacement would change.

ReplaceApplyMessage.description: ReplaceApplyMessage replaces the matches its preview showed; matches is how many that was, so a plan that changed since is not applied.

WelcomeStateMessage.description: WelcomeStateMessage is what the welcome page shows: the shortcut preset and what is indexed.

mac.description: Whether keys are written for a Mac (⌘P) or for Windows and Linux (Ctrl+P)

WelcomeChooseMessage.description: WelcomeChooseMessage saves one choice made on the welcome page in the user's settings.

ParseResultMessage.description: ParseResultMessage drives the chips, diagnostics, completions and toggles.

searchText.description: The text the search runs on when it leaves out the word being completed ("Results for timeout keep updating"). Absent when the whole box is searched.

SearchDoneMessage.description: SearchDoneMessage ends a search: counts, hidden notes, Load more and errors.

revisions.description: For an at: search, the commit each searched repo read, or why it has none (from SearchResult).

folderNotes.description: For a scope Search in Folder wrote, what the folders it names can't give: no file searched (and why), or no commits, being Git repos of their own.

newCommits.description: The shas of the commits a watch found for this query since it last ran, which the results mark New.

PreviewResultMessage.description: PreviewResultMessage fills the preview pane; stale means the result no longer exists.

IndexStatusMessage.description: IndexStatusMessage drives the header dot and indexing banners.

StateRestoreMessage.description: StateRestoreMessage restores the panel's query, recent and pinned queries, and settings.

text.description: The query box's text; absent after a settings change, which leaves the box as it is.

seeded.description: Whether text came from the editor (a selection, or Find Definitions or Find Uses): the box types it in, so ⌘Z brings back what it replaced, and selects it, so typing replaces it.

keepTyping.description: With seeded, for Search in Folder's scope: the box types the text in, so ⌘Z brings back what it replaced, but leaves the cursor at its end, so typing adds to it.

UiSettings.description: UiSettings are the UI-facing settings the host forwards to the webview.

renderWhitespace.description: Which whitespace the preview marks, as editor.renderWhitespace names it; spelunk.ui.renderWhitespace, or editor.renderWhitespace when that is "editor".

tabSize.description: How many spaces wide a tab draws: editor.tabSize.

fontLigatures.description: The CSS font-feature-settings for code, from editor.fontLigatures.

ReplacePlanMessage.description: ReplacePlanMessage is the preview of a replace: the edits it would make, or why it can't.

ReplaceDoneMessage.description: ReplaceDoneMessage says what a replace changed. skipped lists the files left alone because their text no longer matched the index; changed means the matches differed from the preview, so nothing was replaced.

SyntaxLine.description: SyntaxLine is how the color theme colors one line of a file: tokens holds a pair of numbers per token, its start (a UTF-16 offset into text) and its style, which runs to the next token's start. A style is a color's index into the colors of its SyntaxLinesMessage, plus 512 times the token's font style (1 italic, 2 bold, 4 underline, 8 strikethrough); index 0 leaves the text its usual color.

SyntaxLinesMessage.description: SyntaxLinesMessage colors lines of code the panel shows, by their file and text. reset drops every coloring sent before, as when the color theme changes.

colors.description: The theme's colors, as CSS colors, by index; index 0 is unused.

BannerMessage.description: BannerMessage reports daemon health: restarting, stopped or cleared.

Remote.description: Remote is one of a repo's Git remotes: its name and the URL git fetches from (after url.<base>.insteadOf).

FolderNote.description: FolderNote says what a folder picked for Search in Folder can't give: its files aren't searched (skipped, from folder/explain), or, in a history search, its commits aren't (gitRepo).

folder.description: The folder as the note names it: its path, with its repo's name first when several are open, e.g. web-checkout/dist/.

gitRepo.description: The Git repo of its own that holds the folder, named the same way.

SettingsOpenMessage.description: SettingsOpenMessage opens VS Code's Settings at Spelunk's settings, or at one of them.

setting.description: A spelunk.* setting to open Settings at; absent for all of Spelunk's.

FolderExplainParams.description: FolderExplainParams ask about one folder of an open repo: whether its files are searched, and whether it is a Git repo of its own.

path.description: The folder, slash-separated and relative to the repo's root.

FolderExplanation.description: FolderExplanation says why no file in a folder is searched, if none is, and which Git repo inside the open one holds it, if any.

skipped.description: Why no file in the folder is indexed: Git ignores them (.gitignore), index.exclude leaves them out, the folder is reached through a symlink, or it has no files. Absent when some file in it is indexed.

gitRepo.description: The Git repo inside the open one that holds the folder (a submodule or a repo cloned in it), relative to the root: its files are searched, its commits aren't. Absent when the folder is in the open repo's own Git, or outside Git.

SymbolsFindParams.description: SymbolsFindParams ask for the definitions whose names match text, for VS Code's Go to Symbol in Workspace, Go to Definition and Find References.

text.description: What was typed. Its letters must appear in the name in order, ignoring case, unless exact is set. Spaces are ignored; empty text finds nothing.

exact.description: Match the whole name, case and all, as Go to Definition does for the name at the cursor.

limit.description: The most definitions to return, best first: 200 when absent, at most 1000.

includeGeneratedAndVendored.description: Return definitions in generated and vendored files too, marked by rankReason; they are left out when absent.

languageOf.description: An absolute file path: when some definitions found are in that file's language, return only those, and say the language in the result.

SymbolMatch.description: SymbolMatch is one definition symbols/find found: where its name is, what it is, and why it is marked, if it is.

line.description: The 1-based line the definition is on.

column.description: The 1-based column (UTF-16) where the name starts on its line; 1 when the line doesn't spell it out.

rankReason.description: generated or vendored when the file is one, which includeGeneratedAndVendored lets through; absent otherwise.

SymbolsFindResult.description: SymbolsFindResult lists the definitions found, best first.

language.description: The language of languageOf's file, as lang: names it, when the request gave one and Spelunk knows its language.

RepoRemotesParams.description: RepoRemotesParams ask for a repo's Git remotes.

RepoRemotes.description: RepoRemotes are a repo's Git remotes, and the one a link goes to.

git.description: Whether the repo's folder is in a Git repository.

preferred.description: The remote links go to: the one the current branch tracks, else origin, else the only one. Absent when there is none, or several and none of those rules picks one.

LinkParams.description: LinkParams ask what permalinks to results name: the remote, commit, path and lines of each.

refs.description: The results, at most 10,000: the result menu sends one, an export every result it saves.

remote.description: The remote to link to, picked by the user when the repo has several and none is preferred.

LinkProblem.description: LinkProblem is why a result has no permalink: its folder isn't in Git (notGit), the repo has no remote (noRemote) or several and none is preferred (pickRemote), the remote has none of its commits (notPushed), the result's own lines differ from the newest commit the remote has (lineChanged), or its file isn't in that commit (notOnRemote).

Link.description: Link is what a permalink to a result names, or why it has none. The host turns it into the remote's web address. A working-tree result's lines are mapped from the file on disk, as the index has it.

commit.description: The full sha the link points at: a commit result's own; a revision's for an at: result; else HEAD when the remote has it, or the newest commit of the remote's branch that HEAD builds on.

path.description: The file's path in the repository, from its top folder (which may be above the workspace folder), as it is in commit: the old path of a file renamed since.

line.description: The result's first line in commit's file, 1-based; it differs from the line on disk when edits above it aren't in commit.

endLine.description: The result's last line in commit's file, when its match spans lines.

remotes.description: With pickRemote, the remotes to pick from.

Links.description: Links are the permalinks link/resolve worked out, one per ref, in the same order.

RemoteHost.description: RemoteHost is which kind of Git host a repo's links go to, which names the result menu's link items: a known host, other (one Spelunk can't place without the spelunk.permalinks.hosts setting), none (no Git, or no remote), or pick (several remotes; choosing an item asks which).

RepoHost.description: RepoHost is the kind of host one repo's links go to.

RemotesStateMessage.description: RemotesStateMessage tells the panel which kind of host each repo's links go to, for the result menu.

RequestCancelled.when: A newer keystroke cancelled this request

QueryInvalid.when: search/start got a query with error diagnostics

IndexNotReady.when: A repo has no index yet; partial results still stream

RefStale.when: The file or commit behind a ref is gone

IndexCorrupt.when: A shard or database failed a check; a rebuild starts on its own

Overloaded.when: The search hit its time budget and returned what it had
